title: Synthetic document extraction triage cases
description: Clean synthetic probability clouds for demonstrating how Decision-PGA-style decision-state diagnostics can route a document extraction workflow.

scenarios.name: Clean invoice due date
scenarios.document_context: A vendor invoice shows a clearly labeled due date near the payment total.
scenarios.why_it_feels_real: Many extraction tasks are boring in the best way: repeated passes all prefer the same action with only small noise.

scenarios.name: Two plausible contract dates
scenarios.document_context: A contract amendment includes both an effective date and a signature date near the same paragraph.
scenarios.candidate_value: Date field = effective date vs signature date
scenarios.why_it_feels_real: The workflow is not broadly confused. It is mostly choosing between accepting the extracted date and asking which date definition the user intended.

scenarios.name: Missing attachment reference
scenarios.document_context: A purchase request says the approved amount is listed in an attached quote, but only the request cover page is available.
scenarios.candidate_value: Approved amount = value referenced in missing attachment
scenarios.why_it_feels_real: No single next action dominates because the evidence is incomplete. The most useful response is to retrieve the missing page or attachment.

scenarios.name: Near-threshold total
scenarios.document_context: A reimbursement form total is legible, but the extracted value is close to an internal manual-review threshold.
scenarios.why_it_feels_real: The value might be correct, but a small perturbation changes whether the workflow should auto-accept or route to review.

scenarios.name: Contradictory revision packet
scenarios.document_context: A multi-page packet starts with a clean field value, then later pages introduce a revision note and conflicting total.
scenarios.candidate_value: Approved amount = original total vs revised total
scenarios.why_it_feels_real: The right action changes over the read sequence. A workflow should pause and re-evaluate rather than treating the whole packet as one static extraction.
